messages:
ravi: Quick dump from today's fast-kickprefill bring-up for ozma-lite-14b-quant. Goal: shave 10-20ms off 95th pct tail for short-turn chat by inserting a tiny speculative prefill (~4 tokens) when request looks like a short reply.
marie: Nice. Is this different from regular prefetch/prefix-cache?
sam: yeah — kickprefill is request-level and runs before tokenization completes in some clients; basically optimistic tiny prefix to warm KV/cache and fastpath.
noah: what quant config did we run?
ravi: GPTQ 4-bit with per-channel block 128 + residual-fix (q4g128-res). We also tried a q5-like variant for sanity.
sam: config snippet I pushed to bench repo: 
```
--model ozma-lite-14b
--quant q4g128-res
--kickprefill-tokens 4
--kickprefill-threshold 0.65  # score threshold from short-turn classifier
--batching max_tokens=256
```
marie: results summary? numbers please 😅
ravi: baseline (no kickprefill) 95th=238ms, p99=410ms. With kickprefill 95th=218ms, p99=392ms. Mean unchanged. Tail improvement concentrated on requests < 16 tokens.
noah: how about quality delta? any regression on the eval set?
ravi: ran two eval sets: short-chat-sanity (~2k samples) and longform-holdout (~1k). Short-chat BLEU-ish/turn-acc reduced by 0.4% absolute (within noise). Longform unchanged.
eval-bot: run: 2026-03-17T15:03Z id=run_olympus_177001, short-chat delta=-0.4% acc, p=0.12; longform delta=+0.0% acc, p=0.84
sam: that p-value looks noisy. we should add human-review on ~100 short examples focused on hallucination and repetition.
marie: also need to check KV cache drift — if speculative tokens are wrong, downstream decodes could diverge. any evidence?
ravi: instrumented traces show speculative tokens were dropped from final decode in ~18% of cases (i.e., model generated different tokens than speculation). We simulated two modes: speculative-drop (drop speculative KV when mismatch) and speculative-commit (keep). Drop mode had slightly better quality; commit mode was a touch faster but had +0.8% short-chat delta.
noah: operationally, what's the failure mode? increased variance in latency when speculative-commit goes wrong?
ravi: yes, commit can cause wasted KV writes and occasional small decode stalls when we re-roll. But overall still net tail win in our cluster.
marie: can we add a safety gate: only commit when classifier confidence >0.9 and token-likelihood from model > -2.0?
sam: sounds reasonable. Also need rollout plan: canary on 5% traffic, monitor short-chat loss + quality regression metrics and token-level divergence.
noah: ops-bot please schedule a canary: 2026-03-18 08:00 UTC, 5% traffic, group=eng-ml-kickprefill.
ops-bot: scheduled canary: 2026-03-18T08:00:00Z, id=canary_177002. Notifying infra for reserver and tracing hooks.
marie: for eval methodology, let's add a paired A/B holdout: same prompts under commit/drop/none to measure exact divergence and human preference rate. I can set up the HITs if we need humans.
eval-bot: queued paired A/B job id=ab_177003, expected finish: ~4 hours, sample size target=500 per cohort.
ravi: next actions: (1) add confidence gate thresholds and landed config in ops repo, (2) run paired A/B, (3) prepare canary dashboard with token-diff waterfall and short-chat accuracy. Assigning tasks: sam -> dashboard, marie -> human HITs + paired set, noah -> infra knobs for KV rollback, ravi -> landing config + run full quant variant mix.
sam: acked, will stub dashboard widgets and alert for short-chat delta > 1% or p99 increase > 10ms.
marie: I extracted 120 flagged examples where speculation committed and produced different completions — will share in drive for human review.
ravi: thanks all. If canary looks good, we roll to 25% then 100% with staged quorum. Any objections?
noah: none from infra. watch memory churn on dedicated pools.
sam: one more note — bundle also a metric for wasted compute (speculative tokens that were later dropped) so we can compute cost tradeoff.
marie: emoji :thumbsup:
ravi: I'll post a short writeup and link the run artifacts in this thread once uploaded. End of dump.
